# Storage regression snapshot — v1.3.0

Client storage generated at `v1.3.0`, the release of the locale-aware client and of
Token Status List support. Loaded and verified by `TestClientStorageRegressionV1_3_0`.
Regenerate with `TestGenerateClientStorageForRegressionTests` (`GENERATE_STORAGE=1`)
while `version.go` reads `1.3.0`.

This is the first snapshot written *after* the locale rewrite, which is what it exists
to pin. Three storage-visible changes distinguish it from the `v1.0.0` and `v1.1.1`
snapshots:

- **Activity-log text is stored already resolved to a locale**, where the older
  snapshots stored translation maps (`{"en": …, "nl": …}`). Those remain the fixtures
  for the legacy decode path; this one covers the current encode/decode path against a
  real database.
- **OpenID4VCI issuance logs record the issued JWT's `vct`** as the credential id. In
  the older snapshots the issuer metadata's placeholder was stored instead, so all four
  OpenID4VCI issuance entries there read back as `unknown`.
- **Token Status List state exists at rest for the first time.** The snapshot holds a
  `StatusListCredentialSdJwt` whose instances carry a `status.status_list{uri,idx}`
  reference, stored with the INVALID `LastKnownStatus` a revocation left behind, plus a
  cached Status List Token. No older snapshot has any status-list rows at all.

Like `v1.1.1`'s, its `eudi_client_db` is **born encrypted**, so loading it exercises the
steady-state encrypted read path — no plaintext migration runs. The test asserts the
file is not plaintext (`sqlcipher.IsPlaintext` is false).

## Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `bbolt_client_db` | IRMA client bbolt database (idemix credentials, IRMA-issued SD-JWTs, logs). Copied to `db2` on load. |
| `eudi_client_db` | EUDI SQLCipher database (`yivi-eudi.db`): OpenID4VCI credentials, logs, and status-list state. **Encrypted at rest.** |
| `ecdsa_sk.pem` | Client signer key. |
| `keyshare_users.json` | Keyshare users preloaded into the test keyshare server. |
| `metadata.json` | Human-readable dump of the stored credentials and logs. |

Note that `metadata.json` is dumped from the live client that generated the snapshot,
so it shows logo bytes and MIME types that the databases themselves do not hold — the
EUDI database stores only a logo *URI*, while the bytes live in the eudi filesystem,
which is not part of this snapshot. EUDI credentials and log entries therefore load
without an image here.

## Sessions performed

Generated by the same session script as the `v1.0.0` and `v1.1.1` snapshots (see
`TestGenerateClientStorageForRegressionTests`), plus the status-list step, which those
older snapshots predate.

- **IRMA issuance:** `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.fullName` (idemix), `test.test.email`
  (idemix + 10 SD-JWTs), `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.singleton`, `irma-demo.RU.studentCard`.
- **OpenID4VCI issuance:** 3× `TestCredentialSdJwt` (vct `https://localhost:8443/vct/test`)
  and 1× `OrganizationCredentialSdJwt` (vct `https://localhost:8443/vct/organization`, deeply nested).
- **IRMA disclosures:** `test.test.email`; `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.fullName` (×2); and one spanning
  `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.fullName` + `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.singleton` + `irma-demo.RU.studentCard`.
- **IRMA signature.**
- **OpenID4VP disclosures:** `test.test.email` (×2, served from bbolt) plus, via the
  veramo verifier and served from the EUDI DB, `https://localhost:8443/vct/test` (the
  `given_name` and `email` claims) and `https://localhost:8443/vct/organization` (only the
  `university.name` and `university.founded` claims — a subset of the nested tree).
- **Status list:** 1× `StatusListCredentialSdJwt` (vct `https://localhost:8443/vct/statuslist`),
  revoked at the issuer and then refreshed, so the wallet persisted the revocation.
  Revoking is what makes this worth storing: a non-revoked instance's `LastKnownStatus`
  is the zero value, so a snapshot of one would still read correctly if status storage
  broke entirely.
- **Removals** (final actions): `irma-demo.RU.studentCard` + 2 spare `https://localhost:8443/vct/test`.

## Expected database state

- **bbolt** (`bbolt_client_db`): `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.fullName`,
  `irma-demo.MijnOverheid.singleton` and `test.test.email`; the `test.test.email` SD-JWT
  retains 8 of 10 instances (2 consumed by OpenID4VP disclosure); `irma-demo.RU.studentCard` removed.
- **EUDI SQLCipher** (`eudi_client_db`): one `https://localhost:8443/vct/test`, one
  `https://localhost:8443/vct/organization` and one `https://localhost:8443/vct/statuslist`
  batch remaining. The status-list batch is the only one carrying a status reference, and
  it is stored as revoked.
- **Activity logs** (merged from both stores): 22 entries covering all four types —
  issuance, disclosure, signature, removal — returned newest-first, ending with the
  three removals.

## Verified by the regression test

`TestClientStorageRegressionV1_3_0` asserts, entirely through `client.Client`'s public
interface (`GetCredentials` / `LoadNewestLogs`):

- each credential's attribute names and values (including every nested attribute of the
  organization credential), and valid PNG logos on the IRMA credential + issuer images;
- EUDI credential metadata (issuer, SD-JWT format, issuance date, not revoked);
- the `test.test.email` SD-JWT instance count (8 of 10);
- log count, types, newest-first ordering, and content — the disclosed attributes and
  values, the signed message, and the removed credential ids;
- **the format changes above**: that every OpenID4VCI issuance log names the vct it
  issued rather than a placeholder, and that the resolved-string EUDI log rows read back
  with their credential name, issuer name, attribute display names and values intact;
- **the stored status-list state**: that the revoked credential reads back as both
  revoked and revocation-supporting, while a credential with no status reference reads
  back as neither. `GetCredentials` derives both flags from the stored `LastKnownStatus`
  and never goes to the network, so these assertions hold even with the status-list agent
  stopped — the fixture does not depend on the agent still serving that list and index.
  (The *fresh* status-list session in the shared usability check does need the agent, as
  it does for every version's test.)
- that the loaded client can still run fresh sessions: IRMA issuance, IRMA disclosure
  (incl. keyshare) and signature, OpenID4VCI issuance, OpenID4VP disclosure
  (direct-post and veramo), and the status-list issuance/disclosure/revocation flow.

The test removes the stored status-list credential before that last check, so the shared
usability helper starts from the same baseline as the other fixtures: it issues a fresh
status-list credential and expects to disclose a *valid* one, which a second, revoked
candidate of the same vct would get in the way of.
